content:
Sunday will show whatever you left undecided. A Senior Pastor and a Worship Leader can each be ready in their own work and still arrive with different songs, a missing hand-off, and no shared sense of what the gathering is for. Guests do not need a spectacle. They need a service your leaders have actually planned.

This guide is that weekly process. It is not a model order of worship. Your church's approved convictions choose the elements, what they mean, and how long they take. Everyfield will not choose them, write the prayers, or certify the leaders.

---

## Leave the elements with your church

Worship style and service format are church distinctives. [Defining your church values](/wiki/discovery/defining-your-church-values) already treats them that way. Keep that line when you plan Sunday.

Christian worship is always celebrated in a given local cultural setting, and it varies with that local situation. Your plant is one of those settings. A practice that fits another congregation may not belong in yours. Do not add it because a planning chart had an empty row.

The Senior Pastor and the Worship Leader decide together, inside the convictions your church has already approved. If those convictions are still vague, name them before you freeze a running order. A stated philosophy is what keeps the plan from turning into a production packet.

<Callout type="important">
A written plan describes the worship your church has chosen. It does not create that choice. If a meeting starts treating an example as required, stop and ask whether your convictions actually include it.
</Callout>

---

## Plan from the philosophy you have stated

The Worship Leader develops the ministry under the Senior Pastor's direction. [The Worship Leader role](/wiki/launch-team/leadership/worship-leader-role) already calls for a weekly meeting on themes, Scripture, songs, and flow. This article is how that meeting should run.

Open with two sentences you can both say aloud. What is this gathering for, in your church's words? What must not drop out, and what will you refuse to add so the service resembles another church?

Tie the plan to the Worship pillar of the 4 Pillars. Corporate worship is part of loving God, not a warm-up for the announcements. If the page never names Scripture, the prayer your church actually practices, or the aim of the teaching, rewrite it. A new team member should be able to see what you believe you are doing.

<Callout type="insight">
Every church already has a way of gathering, whether or not you use the word liturgy. Write down the way your leaders have chosen. Do not import another church's order to fill the silence.
</Callout>

---

## Hold a weekly planning conversation

Meet at the same time each week, early enough that the team can rehearse what you decided. The Senior Pastor and the Worship Leader are the meeting. Invite someone else only for a piece they own, such as slides or the room, and only for that piece.

Ask the same questions each week.

- [ ] What passage or theme is the Senior Pastor teaching?
- [ ] What must the congregation hear, sing, or pray, given the philosophy you have stated?
- [ ] Which elements from your approved convictions fit this week, and which will you leave out?
- [ ] Who leads each part, and who covers if that person is absent?
- [ ] Which lyrics, recordings, or videos need permission before they reach a screen or a stream?
- [ ] What must rehearsal practice, and what must the room crew know before doors open?

The Senior Pastor owns the teaching and the pastoral aim, including the final say on what the service includes and what it means. The Worship Leader turns that aim into a plan the team can run. Do not hand the conversation to a volunteer thread on Saturday night.

This meeting does not measure calling, character, or fitness to lead. Everyfield does not certify Worship Leaders or gate who may serve. Those judgments stay with your church's own leaders.

Check permissions while the plan can still change. [Copyright licenses for worship and streaming](/wiki/administrative/legal/copyright-licenses-for-worship-and-streaming) is where you sort lyrics, recordings, and video. A file on a laptop is not permission.

<Callout type="warning">
Do not let the song list lead the meeting. Start with the Word the Senior Pastor is bringing and with the philosophy you have already stated. Songs serve that aim. They do not replace it.
</Callout>

---

## Write a running order

A running order is the sequence for this service. It names what happens, who leads it, and what the team needs in hand. It is a tool for the people serving. It is not a theology paper, and it is not a template for the next plant.

Keep it short enough to hold during rehearsal.

- **Service order.** The sequence your leaders chose for this service.
- **Who leads.** The person responsible, and the backup.
- **Team cue.** What the musicians, slides, or room crew must see or hear.
- **Hand-off.** Who moves next, and the words or action that pass it on.
- **Use rights.** Whether a lyric, recording, or video may be used.

Leave a practice off the page if your convictions do not include it. Do not add a sacrament, a set length, or a spoken response because another bulletin had one. This article sets none of those. Your church does.

If corporate prayer belongs in your gathering, name the person who will lead the prayer you have agreed to pray. Do not invent a Prayer Leader office to fill a blank row. Prayer practice and a role title are not the same thing. Do not ask an app to compose the prayer.

<Callout type="tip">
Put the backup name on the same line as the leader. A plan with no cover fails the first week someone is sick, and it fails in the lobby, where you can no longer fix it.
</Callout>

---

## Rehearse the hand-offs

Rehearsal is where the written order meets the people who have to carry it. Practice the start, the hand-offs, and the close. A band that only runs songs will still stumble when the teaching begins or a slide is late.

Give everyone the same page before rehearsal starts. The person on slides should not work from a different list than the Worship Leader. When a cue fails, stop and correct the page. A fix that lives only in memory will not survive next week.

Before Launch Sunday, three team-only Pre-Launch Services are where worship, teaching, and prayer meet the real room. [Pre-Launch Services](/wiki/pre-launch/pre-launch-services) covers that rehearsal and the debrief. Sample times there are a practice schedule for the Launch Team. They are not a public order you must keep after launch.

- [ ] The running order is in every leader's hands before rehearsal.
- [ ] You practice the transitions, not only the music.
- [ ] Slides, sound, and the Worship Leader share one sequence.
- [ ] You correct the page when a cue fails.
- [ ] The room crew knows what must be ready before doors open.

No surprises on Sunday morning. The Senior Pastor and the Worship Leader should already know what the other will do.

---

## Review while it is still fresh

After the gathering, take a few minutes while you still remember what happened. What matched the plan? What surprised either of you? What should not be repeated, and who will change the page before the next meeting?

Do not skip this because you are tired. A note written that day is usable. A note you mean to write on Wednesday usually never appears. Bring it to the next planning conversation. A running order that never changes after a real room is a guess you kept.

---

## Mistakes that become a required order

Watch for these. Each one lets a habit harden into an order nobody approved.

A sample from a conference, a video, or another church becomes "how we do it." Stop that the week it shows up.

The song list is finished before the Senior Pastor names the teaching, so the passage gets bent to fit the set.

The order lives in one person's head. Everyone else guesses. Rehearsal then polishes the music and skips the hand-offs.

The page reads like a concert rundown and never says what the gathering is for. Or someone adds a role title because a chart had an empty box. Do the practice your convictions require. Do not invent an office to satisfy a template.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, with all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with gratefulness in your hearts to God."* — Colossians 3:16 (LSB)
</Callout>

That verse does not give you an order of service. It does name the work the plan should serve. The word of Christ, taught and sung, among the people. Write the order your leaders chose, and rehearse it so the team is not guessing.

title: Planning Worship Services

sources.claim: Colossians 3:16 in the Legacy Standard Bible, quoted in the scripture callout.
sources.quote: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, with all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with gratefulness in your hearts to God.

sources.claim: Christian worship is always celebrated in a given local cultural setting, and one way it relates to culture is by varying with the local situation.
sources.quote: The reality that Christian worship is always celebrated in a given local cultural setting draws our attention to the dynamics between worship and the world's many local cultures.

sources.claim: The Nairobi Statement describes Christian worship as contextual, varying according to the local situation.
sources.quote: Second, it is contextual, varying according to the local situation (both nature and culture).

sources.claim: A church that rejects the label liturgical still has a gathered order, and planning that order is part of preparing worship for that congregation.
sources.publisher: Reformed Worship, Calvin Institute of Christian Worship
sources.quote: every church has a liturgy of some type.

rulings: Bryan ruled B13 = Option A: "Planning process under local leaders" (2026-10-26 1:31 PM ET).
Wording call: kept the backlog title Planning Worship Services. The ruling changes how prescriptive the article is, not the topic name.

Wording call: no model service order, sample sequence, sacrament practice, or required service length. The running-order list names fields to fill, not elements to include. Pre-Launch Service sample times are identified as a team practice schedule, not a public order.

Wording call: corporate prayer is named only when the church's convictions include it. No Prayer Leader title is required, consistent with C05 and C21, which distinguish prayer practice from a title and do not prescribe a service format.
Wording call: sort_order 8, next after published training articles 1 through 7 in seed.json. Section id taken from the training section in seed.json.

Wording call: did not recommend a licensing vendor. Permissions point to the published copyright article. Did not quote the Nairobi Statement's eucharistic shape as Everyfield's order. Used that statement only for the claim that worship is local and contextual.

Wording call: gender-neutral role titles. Everyfield does not choose songs, rotations, liturgy, or prayers, does not schedule recurring post-launch worship, and does not judge calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health.
